question.latex: Consider the matrices $A = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -2 \\ 4 & -2 \end{bmatrix}$ and $B = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 9 \\ 1 & 3 \end{bmatrix}$. If matrices $P$ and $Q$ are such that $PA = B$ and $AQ = B$, then the absolute value of the sum of the diagonal elements of $2$P + Q$$ is:
question.unicode: Consider the matrices A = begin{bmatrix} 2 & -2  4 & -2 end{bmatrix} and B = begin{bmatrix} 3 & 9  1 & 3 end{bmatrix}. If matrices P and Q are such that PA = B and AQ = B, then the absolute value of the sum of the diagonal elements of 2P + Q is:
question.plainText: Consider the matrices A = begin{bmatrix} 2 & -2 4 & -2 end{bmatrix} and B = begin{bmatrix} 3 & 9 1 & 3 end{bmatrix}. If matrices P and Q are such that PA = B and AQ = B, then the absolute value of the sum of the diagonal elements of 2P + Q is:

explanation.latex:
$|A| = -4 - (-8) = 4 
eq 0$, so $A$ is invertible.
$A^{-1} = \frac{1}{4}\begin{bmatrix} -2 & 2 \\ -4 & 2 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} -1/2 & 1/2 \\ -1 & 1/2 \end{bmatrix}$.
$P = B A^{-1} \implies Tr(P) = Tr(B A^{-1})$.
$Q = A^{-1} B \implies Tr(Q) = Tr(A^{-1} B) = Tr(B A^{-1}) = Tr(P)$.
Calculate $P = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 9 \\ 1 & 3 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} -1/2 & 1/2 \\ -1 & 1/2 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} -21/2 & 6 \\ -7/2 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$.
$Tr(P) = -21/2 + 2 = -17/2$.
$Tr(2(P + Q)) = 2[Tr(P) + Tr(Q)] = 4 Tr(P) = 4(-17/2) = -34$.
Absolute value is $|-34| = 34$.
